hero.label: Wrocław → Prague
hero.intro: Wrocław to Prague by private chauffeur is a 285 km door-to-door transfer south through the Kłodzko valley and over the border at Náchod, around three hours of driving. Prestigo’s fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes-Benz E-Class, tolls and the Czech motorway vignette included. Pickup from any Wrocław address, Wrocław Główny or Wrocław Airport (WRO), drop-off anywhere in Prague.
hero.imageAlt: Private chauffeur transfer from Wrocław to Prague in a Mercedes

openingParagraphs: A private transfer from Wrocław to Prague covers about 285 km — south out of the city toward Kłodzko, across the Czech border at Kudowa-Zdrój and Náchod, then on to Hradec Králové and the D11 motorway into Prague — and takes around three hours door to door. The fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers; groups of up to 6 travel in the V-Class from €{vPrice}; the S-Class is available from €{sPrice} for executive or VIP travel. Your chauffeur collects you from your hotel near the Rynek, from Wrocław Główny or from Arrivals at Wrocław Airport, and drops you at the door of your Prague hotel, apartment or office.

The fare is set when you book and does not change: fuel, tolls, the Czech motorway vignette, bottled water, Wi-Fi and child seats on request are all included. There is no fast direct train on this route — a private car is the simplest way to get from Lower Silesia to a Prague doorstep.

paragraphs: From a pickup near the Rynek, on Ostrów Tumski or at Wrocław Airport, your chauffeur leaves the city southbound on the S8 expressway and continues through the Kłodzko valley, with the Sudetes rising on both sides. The road passes below the fortress at Kłodzko and climbs gently to the spa town of Kudowa-Zdrój.

The border between Kudowa-Zdrój and Náchod sits inside the Schengen Area: no routine check, no queue, only a change of language on the road signs and Náchod’s château above the town. On the Czech side the road runs west to Hradec Králové, where it joins the D11 motorway for the final stretch across the Elbe lowlands to Prague. Total distance is approximately 285 kilometres; driving time is about three hours. Weekend traffic at the border can add 15–20 minutes.

Your chauffeur checks the route before departure. If the Náchod crossing is slow, they can take the northern line through Liberec instead — a little longer, but steady. You arrive in Prague with the day still in hand: time to check in, then out to Vinohrady or the Old Town for the evening.

dayTrip.intro: The road from Wrocław to Prague runs through hill country with a castle or fortress every half hour. Three stops cover most requests.

configurations.title: Kłodzko Fortress
configurations.body: Leave Wrocław at 9:00 and stop in Kłodzko after about an hour and a quarter — the fortress walls, the view over the valley and the stone bridge in the old town. Back on the road and in Prague by mid-afternoon.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: Náchod Château
configurations.body: Just over the border, Náchod’s château looks down on the town square. An hour for the courtyards and gardens, or a coffee on the square, then two hours on to Prague.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: Lunch in Hradec Králové
configurations.body: Hradec Králové is about an hour and a half from Prague, where the road meets the D11. Lunch on the Great Square in the old town, then a straight run on the motorway to your Prague door.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

dayTrip.footnote: Stops are planned at booking and priced by the extra time and distance — tell us where you would like to stop and we confirm a firm quote before you book. A short coffee or rest stop on the way is always included.

chauffeurNarrative: Your chauffeur arrives at your Wrocław hotel at the agreed time and comes to the door. At Wrocław Airport they wait inside Arrivals with your name and take the luggage from the belt to the car.

Three hours through the Sudetes is a calm drive. Work, rest or watch the hills — your chauffeur takes the cue. If you would like to know where you are staying in Prague and what is worth seeing nearby, ask: Prague is where they live.
Water, charger and Wi-Fi are in the cabin. A stop in Kłodzko or a coffee in Náchod is a sentence away. On arrival your bags go to reception with you.

items.title: Agreed before you leave
items.body: Fuel, tolls, the Czech vignette and the chauffeur’s time are inside the fare. Nothing is added in Prague.

items.title: The direct way
items.body: Rail between Wrocław and Prague is slow and often involves changes. One car takes you from your Wrocław door to your Prague door, luggage loaded once.

items.title: Prague-based, Prague-run
items.body: Prestigo is a Prague company with its own Mercedes fleet. Your chauffeur knows the city you are arriving in — the hotel entrances, the restricted Old Town streets, the quickest way to your address.

faqs.q: How long does a private transfer from Wrocław to Prague take?
faqs.a: About three hours door to door: south through Kłodzko to the border at Kudowa-Zdrój and Náchod, then via Hradec Králové and the D11 into Prague. Busy weekends at the border can add 15–20 minutes.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi or chauffeur from Wrocław to Prague?
faqs.a: A fixed fare from €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers, €{vPrice} in the V-Class for up to 6, or €{sPrice} in the S-Class. Fuel, tolls, the Czech motorway vignette and the chauffeur’s time are included — per car, not per person.

faqs.q: Can you pick me up at Wrocław Airport or Wrocław Główny?
faqs.a: Yes. Give us your flight number and your chauffeur tracks the landing at Wrocław Airport, waits inside Arrivals with your name and drives you straight to Prague. Pickups at Wrocław Główny or any hotel are arranged the same way.

faqs.q: Is a private transfer better than the train or bus from Wrocław to Prague?
faqs.a: There is no fast direct train, and rail journeys usually take longer than the drive with at least one change. Long-distance buses run the route and are the cheapest option for a solo traveller with light bags. A private transfer is door to door, leaves when you want and costs the same for one passenger or three.

faqs.q: Can we stop on the way from Wrocław to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Kłodzko, Náchod and Hradec Králové are the usual requests. Tell us at booking and we include the stop in a fixed quote. A short coffee or rest break is always included.

faqs.q: Do I need my passport between Poland and the Czech Republic?
faqs.a: Both countries are in the Schengen Area, so there is no routine border control at Kudowa-Zdrój and Náchod. Carry your passport or EU ID card anyway — spot checks happen, and non-EU travellers must have their documents with them.

relatedRoutesIntro: Wrocław to Prague is often one leg of a longer trip through Poland and Bohemia. Clients arriving from Kraków, Warsaw or Hradec Králové book the same way — one car, one fixed fare, drop-off at the door in Prague.
